summary.intent: Check whether phase 73 (cipher-box GSD roadmap) had open discussion points before planning, then kick off /gsd-plan-phase for it — ensuring the feature branch is named correctly (not a stray planner-generated branch) and that any tangential pending todos get folded into scope.
summary.outcome: Confirmed phase 73 was plan-ready, created and committed to the correct branch (feat/shared-write-navigation-correctness-web), folded two tangential todos into the ROADMAP, and ran the full plan-phase pipeline (research → VALIDATION.md → pattern-mapping → 9 PLAN.md files across 3 waves). Plan-checker found 2 blockers + 1 warning; fixes were applied directly and a re-verification commit was in progress when the transcript ended.

repo: cipher-box's GSD branch_template is 'feat/{slug}'; the correct slug is the phase directory name minus the leading number (e.g. phase 72's dir → feat/sdk-write-plane-durability-and-correctness), not the stray docs/plan-phase-{N} branch the planner can spin up.

plan-phase.md workflow has an explicit Step 0 guardrail: 'Do not create, rename, or switch git branches during plan-phase' — so pre-creating and committing to the correct feature branch before invoking the skill reliably prevents branch drift.

plan:pre hooks active in this repo: intel, research, pattern-mapper, schema-gate→planner, tdd→planner, drift-gate. schema-gate only fires for TypeORM entity/migration file changes, not SDK/web hook changes.
fetchShareKeys must be preserved even when removing the dead folder-IPNS write-share-key path — only that specific path is dead code, not the whole function (SC7 landmine identified during research).
intel's API-SURFACE.md regeneration can legitimately produce 0 symbols (HINT-only) for phases whose real grounding lives in RESEARCH.md/PATTERNS.md rather than a stable public API surface.

code.finding: Never calls runWithFailureUx at all — a real API 410 (tombstone) currently surfaces as an uncaught AxiosError instead of a classified failure. Root cause was deeper than the originating WRITE-03 todo stated; research locked plan sequencing to SC7→SC6→SC1+SC2→SC4 to fix this properly.

TDD RED-task verify command piped test output through `grep ... || true`, which swallows the real exit code and makes the 'confirm RED' gate unable to ever fail — a recurring anti-pattern the plan-checker flagged as a blocker.
Same grep-masks-exit-code RED-gate anti-pattern as 73-02-PLAN.md; fixed by inverting on the test's actual exit code.
depends_on frontmatter was missing an implied ordering dependency on 73-05 (had only [73-07, 73-01]); added without changing its wave assignment.

workflow: When scanning a large pending-todo backlog (51 items) for tangential relevance to a phase's scope, delegate the classification to a subagent rather than reading each todo directly — preserves main-context budget.

Plan-checker (gsd-plan-checker) blockers that are mechanical/fully-specified (like an exit-code-masking test pattern) are cheaper to fix directly than to re-run a full gsd-planner cycle; only structural/judgment-level findings warrant a replan.
TaskCreate/TaskUpdate was used to track the multi-stage plan-phase pipeline (research → validation → pattern-map → plan → verify) as discrete checkable steps across long-running subagent spawns.

friction: Phase 73 had no directory, DISCUSSION.md, or discuss-phase artifacts yet, requiring manual cross-checking of ROADMAP.md, STATE.md, and source todo files just to confirm it was plan-ready.

Had to proactively guard against a known risk (gsd-planner sometimes creates a stray docs/plan-phase-{N} branch instead of the intended feat/ branch) by reading the workflow file to confirm the Step 0 no-branch-switching gate would hold.

Plan-checker's first pass surfaced 2 blockers and 1 warning (same RED-gate anti-pattern duplicated across two plan files, plus a missing depends_on), requiring a manual fix-and-reverify loop rather than a clean first-pass approval.
open_items: Re-run gsd-plan-checker to confirm the PASS gate after applying the 3 fixes (73-02, 73-04, 73-09 PLAN.md edits) — not yet confirmed complete at end of transcript.

STATE.md's open Q1 (Phase 68) — whether a co-writer offline during write-key rotation needs an explicit re-fetch requirement vs. grace/notification — remains unresolved and is tangential to the SC4 wire-end-to-end decision just locked for phase 73.

Three 'adjacent-but-separate' pending todos (SDK merge parity, dead SDK scaffolding retirement, ESLint boundary rule) were explicitly left out of phase 73's folded-in scope; deferred rather than resolved.
SHARE-WRITE-KEY write-share key threading gap (noted in existing project memory) remains open and is adjacent to the shared-write navigation work phase 73 is doing.
